sector_model: insurer (Florida homeowners P&C, reciprocal-style reinsurance dependent); use earnings, book value, reserves, catastrophe and reinsurance; no FCF model
thesis: HCI Group (Florida-focused property insurer) reported nine-month 2026 net income of 230.7M (vs 201.4M), diluted EPS 17.48, equity 1,121.3M and small debt (31.8M carrying amount). At 186.03 it trades near 7.0x TTM net income (7.5x TTM diluted EPS of 24.73) and 2.1x book, a low multiple for that earnings level, with 80.0M of 2026 buybacks.
counterthesis: A single-state hurricane exposure can erase several years of earnings, and a low P/E on peak profits is typical for property insurers late in a favorable cat cycle. Net premiums earned are only +12.6% in 9M26 vs a year earlier and flat sequentially (219.1M Q3 vs 219.0M Q2); unearned premiums rose, but cash and equivalents fell from 1,210M to 744M (partly to buybacks and investments, uncertain). Shares fell 8.1% from 11-04 to 11-06 after the Q3 10-Q, cause not established. Combined ratio, reinsurance tower cost and reserve development were NOT read, so the earnings quality cannot be judged yet.
invalidation: Large Florida hurricane loss or reinsurance tower failure, adverse reserve development, Florida market softening that lowers premiums and margins, or evidence that 2026 earnings were boosted by unusually light cat losses or reserve releases.
